clue.text: Hawkish observation of the underworld?

parts.note: a hawk looking down sees the world below it, the 'under-world', from high above, which is the sight a map or aerial picture gives

explanation.surface: A grim look at gangland, or at Hades, by someone of warlike views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawkish' looks political and 'underworld' suggests crime or Hades; read literally, a bird of prey looks down at the world lying under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from directly overhead, as a flying bird would have, is the phrase for an aerial or overall perspective.

clue.text: Where counsel strive to win agreement

parts.note: barristers (counsel) argue their cases at the bar of a court
to win is to gain

explanation.surface: Barristers fighting to secure a deal for their client.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal struck between two parties is an agreement on terms.

clue.text: Pulled together and recovered strength

definitions.meaning: troops ... when they regrouped and united
a patient or market ... when it picked up after a weakness

explanation.surface: A team regrouped and found its second wind.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is both to regroup in unity and to revive after decline, as a sick person or falling share price does.

clue.text: Often a post-wedding command to smile and snap out of it

definitions.text: Often a post-wedding command to smile and snap out of it

parts.words: Often a post-wedding command to smile and snap out of it
parts.note: the photographer at a wedding tells the group what to utter so they grin, then takes the 'snap'; 'snap out of it' pretends to mean cheer up

explanation.surface: Someone sulking after the ceremony is told to smile and pull themselves together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap out of it' reads as 'stop moping', but here the snap is the photograph taken out of the smiling group.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask subjects to utter this dairy word because it forces the mouth into a smile.

clue.text: A linesman much respected by Dublin players

definitions.text: A linesman much respected by Dublin players

parts.words: A linesman much respected by Dublin players
parts.note: a 'linesman' is taken as a writer of lines of verse, an Irish poet who co-founded the Abbey Theatre whose actors are the Dublin players

explanation.surface: A football official popular with an Irish team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' and 'players' suggest a match official and a sports team; the linesman is a poet and the players are actors at Dublin's Abbey Theatre, which he helped found.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats, the Irish poet, wrote many lines of verse and helped found Dublin's national theatre.

clue.text: He canvassed the famous beard

definitions.meaning: a painter covering canvases, the Flemish portraitist Anthony van Dyck, anglicised
the short pointed beard seen in that painter's portraits is named after him

explanation.surface: A politician out canvassing votes with a well-known beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvassed' suggests seeking votes; it means painted on canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter Van Dyck worked on canvas, and the neat pointed beard in his portraits bears his name.

clue.text: Cathedral city — I go into total heaven

parts.note: Ely is the Cambridgeshire city famous for its cathedral

indicators.note: the letter for I is said to go into the word for total, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a total is a sum

explanation.surface: A visitor to a cathedral city finds it complete bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a small cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was the paradise where the blessed lived after death.

clue.text: One of original 12 getting a little scoop that could make a stir

definitions.text: One of original 12 getting a little scoop that could make a stir

parts.words: One of original 12 getting a little scoop that could make a stir
parts.note: one of Christ's twelve disciples combined with a small scooping utensil used for stirring tea, a traditional christening gift

explanation.surface: One of the first twelve lands a minor news exclusive that causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoop' and 'make a stir' suggest journalism; the scoop is a small spoon and the stir is of a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon whose handle ends in a figure of one of the twelve disciples, traditionally given at christenings.

clue.text: Saucy stuff picked by society in conference

indicators.note: the letter for society is placed in the word for conference

parts.note: a parley is a conference between opposing sides

explanation.surface: Something cheeky singled out by a club at its meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' suggests cheeky; it means a herb used to make a white sauce served with fish or ham.
explanation.definitionFit: This green herb is a classic base for a sauce, so it is stuff that goes into sauce.

clue.text: Newton 016 day terribly vexed

indicators.note: terribly shows the letters are badly arranged and must be rearranged

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
the newspaper OCR has read the word one as the digits 016, so it stands for the letters of one

explanation.surface: Newton has an awful day and is irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed '016' is an OCR misreading of 'one'; rearranging N, ONE and DAY gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexed and irritated are synonyms for being put out.

clue.text: Some loafers enjoy a Jutland spread

definitions.text: Some loafers enjoy a Jutland spread

parts.words: Some loafers enjoy a Jutland spread
parts.note: 'loafers' are taken as loaves of bread, and the spread is a dairy product from Jutland in Denmark

explanation.surface: Idlers relax with a lavish meal laid out in Jutland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loafers' looks like idlers and 'spread' a feast; loaves get spread with the butter Denmark exports.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter from Denmark, whose mainland is the Jutland peninsula, is a well-known export spread on bread.

clue.text: Abject prodigal tacking on to saint

indicators.note: the word for prodigal is tacked onto the saint, so it follows it

parts.note: prodigal means wastefully lavish

explanation.surface: A wretched spendthrift latches onto a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prodigal' brings the returning son to mind; here it just means extravagant.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject means servile and grovelling, utterly submissive.

clue.text: Staying out for underworld runner

definitions.note: the definition is the river of the underworld, the answer the adjective describing it

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stays away rather than become a gangster's runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is crossword shorthand for a river; the underworld's river is the Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of the Styx, the river that flows through Hades in Greek myth.

clue.text: Ruled through Stalin edict

indicators.note: the answer runs through the words, held across them

explanation.surface: A dictator's decree governed everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled paper has lines printed on it.

clue.text: New pride in jerrybuilt semi holding flesh and blood together

indicators.note: the rearranged first word is placed in the rearranged second
jerrybuilt means shoddily assembled, so the letters are put together badly
new means the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Pride in a shoddy new semi-detached house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flesh and blood' suggests family, but the skin is what holds the body's tissue in. 'New' and 'jerrybuilt' each signal their own anagram, and 'in' nests one result (PIDER) inside the other (EMIS).
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer of skin wraps and contains the body's tissue.

clue.text: Nasty trait, breaking into anger on Sunday, that upsets one

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after
the rearranged letters break into the word for anger, sitting inside it

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty habit flares into Sunday fury and upsets someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty' signals an anagram giving RITAT; 'breaking into' puts it inside the word for anger, and in a down clue 'on' sets Sunday's letter beneath. The definition reads as a verb phrase: something irritates when it upsets one.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy or get on someone's nerves is to bother them.

clue.text: A third of a pint, perhaps? Not worth bothering about

definitions.text: A third of a pint, perhaps?
definitions.meaning: a third of a pint is a little measure of ale

explanation.surface: A tiny drink is hardly worth the fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is literal: a modest quantity of ale; the phrase also means a trifling matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a weak or modest ale, and idiomatically anything trivial or unimportant.

clue.text: Highly independent Spanish neighbours met here

definitions.text: Highly independent Spanish neighbours met here

parts.words: Highly independent Spanish neighbours met here
parts.note: a tiny independent state high in the Pyrenees, where Spain and its neighbour France meet

explanation.surface: Very self-reliant Spaniards got together with the people next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly' refers to the mountains, and the principality lies where Spain meets its neighbour France.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sovereign principality sits high in the Pyrenees between Spain and France.

clue.text: Drink to the airforce unit's bird

parts.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does
a wing is a unit of an air force

explanation.surface: A toast to the squadron's mascot bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit is a crested plover, a type of wading bird.

clue.text: Digital project on hand

parts.note: 'digital' is read as to do with digits, the fingers, and 'project' as a verb, to stick out on the hand

explanation.surface: A computer job currently under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital project' looks like a computing task; it is a digit that projects from the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The short thick digit that sticks out from the side of the hand.

clue.text: Is he progressing on an engine-driver's course?

definitions.text: Is he progressing on an engine-driver's course?

parts.words: Is he progressing on an engine-driver's course?
parts.note: 'course' suggests a railway track, but it is a course of instruction followed by a learner

explanation.surface: A question about whether a locomotive driver is making headway along his route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engine-driver's course' reads as a railway line; the pun is on train, to instruct.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner being instructed in a skill; this one would literally be 'trained'.

clue.text: United Nations test that isn't healthy

parts.note: to sound out is to test or probe

explanation.surface: A UN inspection reveals poor health.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound means not in good health or condition, unreliable.

clue.text: I posed "" complex to keep psychiatrists busy

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'I posed "" complex to keep psychiatrists busy': a quoted piece is missing between the quote marks; I POSED gives only six of OEDIPUS's letters, and no reprint was found.
annotationWithheld.clue: I posed "" complex to keep psychiatrists busy

clue.text: Booking Francoise?

parts.note: Francoise is a French novelist's first name, and 'booking' suggests a long tale or book, the four-letter word for one plus a last letter

explanation.surface: Reserving a table for a Frenchwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: Francoise Sagan was the French author of 'Bonjour Tristesse'; 'Booking' hints at SAGA, a long story.
explanation.definitionFit: Francoise Sagan was a French novelist, so a 'booking' Francoise is one who wrote books.

clue.text: In this the goods should be on the way

definitions.text: In this the goods should be on the way

parts.words: In this the goods should be on the way
parts.note: goods 'in' this state are being carried between places, en route to the customer

explanation.surface: A customer is told the order is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchandise being carried from supplier to buyer is said to be in passage.

clue.text: Tending to chant after the railway workers

indicators.note: the word for chant comes after the union's letters

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, the British railway workers' union
to chant is to sing

explanation.surface: A protest song started by striking rail staff.
explanation.walkthrough: NUR is the old British National Union of Railwaymen.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring for or looking after the sick is the work of tending them.

clue.text: All-round cut under the Brotherhood

parts.note: a haircut shaved in a ring, as worn by members of a monastic brotherhood

explanation.surface: Sweeping cuts imposed by a secretive fraternity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-round cut' suggests budget cuts; it is a hairstyle, a ring of hair round a shaven crown, worn by monks.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaved crown with a fringe of hair around it marks a monk or cleric.

clue.text: A hone gnashed in frustration — against the wall

indicators.note: the letters are thrown about in frustration, rearranged

explanation.surface: Teeth grinding at a bone in frustration when cornered.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'bone' is an OCR misreading of 'hone', which supplies the second H.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pushed to the wall and beaten looks down in shame and defeat.
